dispositions.statement: The equity rows without a unit count are the two Metropolis Technologies preferred lines (16.00 % and 17.50 %). Footnote 1 of each filing says the 'Par Amount/Units' column holds a par amount in thousands for debt and preferred equity and a unit amount only for Other Equity; the filer tags the preferred figure (4,320 and 480) with the principal concept. So no unit count is printed for these rows, and none is published. Every Other Equity row in these quarters now publishes its unit count (this run: 'Other Equity' classed as equity, the 2025-03-31 counts set to the printed figures), which raises the coverage to 2 of 4, 3 of 5 and 3 of 5; the check wants 70 pct. The preferred par itself is not published either: the shared holdings step clears principal_amount on every preferred-equity row (pipeline/unified_holdings.py, tests TestEquityPrincipalAmountNulled), so the printed par 4,320 / 480 thousand is an unpublished figure, parked as observation preferred-units-column-is-a-face-amount for an owner ruling; it is not a unit count and C04 counts unit counts only. At 2025-09-30 the same footnote holds, but the filer tagged the two preferred pars as share counts (InvestmentOwnedBalanceShares 4320 and 480) and the build published them as unit counts; those two counts were withdrawn by context-keyed row corrections (D-244), which leaves 4 of 6 equity rows with a unit count (66.7 pct, below 70 pct). The four are the Other Equity lines (Rapyd 80,991, BusBud 178,935, Metropolis 280, Mews 19,200), as printed. From 2025-12-31 the filer prints the 17.50 % line as 480,000 units and tags a share count; those quarters pass. No fix applies: publishing the par as a unit count would be wrong.

dispositions.statement: The filer prints its ratio of net investment income to average net assets for the year to date and says it is not annualised. The company-facts step splits that running ratio into quarters, so income_yield_pct holds one quarter's unannualised ratio (1.29 to 2.04), while distribution_rate is annualised (5.3 to 9.8). F16 compares the two, so it fails whenever the fund pays out near its income. On a like basis the quarters pass: distributions per share 0.26, 0.31, 0.45, 0.48, 0.48 against net investment income per share 0.30, 0.42, 0.41, 0.42, 0.42 (the 2025-06-30 six-month figure 0.84 less 0.42). No fix applies at fund level; the check's two inputs are on different bases.
